title: 1950 AHSME Problem 49
statement: A triangle has a fixed base \(AB\) that is \(2\) inches long. The median from \(A\) to side \(BC\) is \(1\dfrac12\) inches long and can have any position emanating from \(A.\) The locus of the vertex \(C\) of the triangle is:

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text: A circle with \(A\) as center and radius \(2\) inches

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text: A circle with \(A\) as center and radius \(3\) inches

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text:
A circle with radius \(3\) inches and center
\(4\) inches from \(B\) along \(BA\)

solutions.text:
Put \(A\) at the origin and regard \(B,\) \(C,\) and the midpoint \(M\) of \(BC\) as vectors. Since \(AM=\tfrac32,\) the point \(M\) moves on a circle of radius \(\tfrac32\) centered at \(A.\) The midpoint relation gives \[ C=2M-B. \] Thus the locus of \(C\) is the image of that circle under a dilation by \(2\) followed by translation by \(-B.\) It is a circle of radius \(3\) centered at \(-B.\)

Because \(AB=2,\) the point \(-B\) is \(4\) inches from \(B\) along the ray \(BA.\) Hence the correct answer is D.
hints: Let \(M\) be the midpoint of \(BC\); then \(M\) moves on a circle centered at \(A\)
In vector form, the midpoint relation gives \(\vec C=2\vec M-\vec B\) when \(A\) is the origin
